contradicting_evidence: Mid-alt proxy mean performance of approximately -0.95% is better than BTC's approximately -1.65%, and a slight majority of the small-alt proxy outperformed BTC. This is relative resilience, not broad outright recovery.
ETH's falling hourly open interest and negative anchor funding leave room for a relief rebound rather than uninterrupted selling.
The ETF evidence covers one settled session, so continuing redemptions are not established.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: A choppy downward bias is favored, with relief rallies vulnerable unless price repair is accompanied by stronger ETH/BTC and broader participation. Existing flow and liquidity headwinds weigh against assuming that stabilization will become continuation higher.
falsification_conditions: A sustained multi-session BTC and ETH recovery is accompanied by improving ETH/BTC and broad gains across the observed capitalization proxies.
Fresh settled ETF sessions show a durable improvement in demand while price holds its recovery.
Updated stablecoin observations show contraction easing alongside actual participation improvement; supply stabilization alone would be insufficient.
missing_evidence: Subsequent settled ETF sessions and a fresh stablecoin-supply update are unavailable.
There is no multi-day breadth or ETH/BTC sequence confirming persistence or reversal.
The supplied macro levels lack recent changes and cannot establish a fresh 72h macro impulse.
supporting_evidence: The final November 9 ETF session recorded net outflows of $201.0 million for BTC and $184.6 million for ETH.
Stablecoin supply contracted approximately 0.34% over one day, 1.58% over seven days and 4.61% over 30 days; deployment confirmation is not established.
Weak breadth spans all observed capitalization proxies in outright returns: large-, mid- and small-alt median 24h returns are negative.
ETH fell approximately 3.39% over 24h versus BTC's 1.65% decline, and the latest ETH/BTC hour also declined, weakening the case for transmission beyond BTC.
